risk_surfaces: Silent behavior change for existing deployers who set HARNESS_MODEL intending it to steer claude_code or codex: that was honored before this commit (cascade applied to all runtimes), now it is ignored and roles fall back to runtime base defaults (sonnet/haiku; codex auth-mode default). No warning or log is emitted at any call site (schemas.py:733-734, resolve.go:247-249), so production model choices change invisibly on upgrade.

Docker-image-baked value now becomes load-bearing twice: it feeds opencode.json small_model interpolation (Dockerfile:57) AND, for open_code, the entire role cascade via HARNESS_MODEL. The drift guard (tests/test_model_config.py:603-629) pins only the string equality with _OPENROUTER_AUTO_DEFAULT_MODEL, but nothing couples the Go constant openRouterAutoDefaultModel (go/internal/config) to the Python _OPENROUTER_AUTO_DEFAULT_MODEL - the two languages duplicate the model id as independent literals (config_test.go:208 hardcodes 'openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731'), so a Python-side bump of the auto default will pass Python tests against a stale Go constant until the cross-language Dockerfile guard happens to run.

String-literal scoping duplicated in two languages: 'HARNESS_MODEL' is matched positionally inside the _DEFAULT_MODEL_ENV_VARS/defaultModelEnvVars tuples and 'open_code' as a bare literal. Reordering the tuple (HARNESS_MODEL is intentionally LAST so it only wins when the first two are unset) or renaming the env var breaks the skip logic silently rather than loudly; there is no shared constant for the runtime string in either scoping branch.

Runtime normalization asymmetry: resolve_runtime_models validates runtime against _RUNTIME_BASE_MODELS before calling the cascade (schemas.py:891-894, resolve.go:360-367), so the open_code comparison there is safe; but _default_model_from_env is also imported and called directly from the fast path (swe_af/fast/schemas.py:188) with config.runtime. Python safety rests on the Pydantic Literal['claude_code','open_code','codex'] (fast/schemas.py:127); the Go FastBuildConfig is a plain struct (fastconfig.go:87-101) where a zero-value FastBuildConfig{} constructed without LoadFastBuildConfig has Runtime=="" -> HARNESS_MODEL silently skipped. Existing code paths all go through LoadFastBuildConfig/defaultFastBuildConfig, but nothing enforces it.

Dockerfile drift guard is text-format brittle: _dockerfile_value (tests/test_model_config.py:607-613) requires a line starting exactly 'ENV HARNESS_MODEL=' (unquoted, no spaces around =). Reformatting to 'ENV HARNESS_MODEL="..."' or a multi-var ENV line makes the guard raise AssertionError (false failure) or miss the value (it raises if no line found - safe direction), and any future build-arg indirection (ARG HARNESS_MODEL) bypasses it entirely.

Cross-suite coupling: the Python test suite now asserts on go/Dockerfile contents (test_go_image_matches_default, tests/test_model_config.py:625-629). If go/ is ever split out of the monorepo or the Python tests run from a checkout without go/, this fails for reasons unrelated to Python behavior; conversely the Go suite has no equivalent guard, so 'cd go && make check' (the canonical Go check) alone does not protect the Go image's baked value.

Error paths unchanged but precedence-adjacent: the cascade still returns first non-empty stripped value, and _default_planning_model/_default_planning_model precedence (SWE_MODEL_HIGH -> env -> base) is preserved (schemas.py:790-813 docstring, resolve.go:270-288). However Go DefaultPlanningModel falls back to openRouterAutoDefaultModel/'sonnet' directly rather than through ResolveRuntimeModels; it inherits the new scoping only because it calls defaultModelFromEnv(DefaultRuntime()) (resolve.go:281). A future refactor that reverts DefaultRuntime() to a hardcoded runtime would silently change which env vars steer planning - the scoping correctness depends on call-site discipline in three places per language.

Test environment sensitivity: new Python tests build a fully cleared env via mock.patch.dict(..., clear=True) with only the cascade vars re-set (tests/test_model_config.py:414-417, 432-436, 450-454). If provider-selection vars (OPENROUTER_API_KEY etc.) later influence _codex_default_model/_openrouter_only_env branches in ways the cleared env doesn't anticipate, these tests encode 'no provider env' assumptions implicitly; the Go tests rely on clearProviderEnv(t) covering the same set - any new env var added to the cascade must be added to both helpers or the contract tests pass vacuously.
pr_narrative: Two coupled fixes shipped as one commit (0c64fe7, PR #142), both about the HARNESS_MODEL environment variable. OLD MECHANISM: (1) Both Dockerfiles baked ENV HARNESS_MODEL=openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Dockerfile:68 old, go/Dockerfile:131 old) purely so OpenCode's opencode.json small_model {env:HARNESS_MODEL} interpolation always resolved. (2) HARNESS_MODEL was the third, last-wins step of the deployer env cascade SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL -> AI_MODEL -> HARNESS_MODEL in _default_model_from_env() (swe_af/execution/schemas.py:709) and defaultModelFromEnv() (go/internal/config/resolve.go:237), consulted for EVERY runtime. Combined effect: any image-baked HARNESS_MODEL value leaked into model resolution. Consequence A: OpenRouter-only open_code deployments silently ran kimi-k2.6 instead of the documented auto default _OPENROUTER_AUTO_DEFAULT_MODEL=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731. Consequence B: claude_code/codex Docker deployments received the baked openrouter/... id, which those CLIs cannot consume (README documented the resulting codex PM failure in ~13s instead of fixing it). NEW MECHANISM: (1) Both Dockerfiles now bake openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (Dockerfile:73, go/Dockerfile:137). (2) The cascade function now takes a runtime parameter and skips HARNESS_MODEL unless runtime == 'open_code' (swe_af/execution/schemas.py:709-733, go/internal/config/resolve.go:245-253). SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL and AI_MODEL remain runtime-agnostic. All call sites updated: resolve_runtime_models passes its validated runtime (schemas.py:914, resolve.go:388); the fast path now passes config.runtime instead of nothing (swe_af/fast/schemas.py:188, go/internal/config/fastconfig.go:144); _default_planning_model routes through resolve_runtime_models with a normalized runtime (schemas.py:805->914) and Go DefaultPlanningModel uses DefaultRuntime() (resolve.go:281). Supporting changes: README.md:406 and .env.example:47-90 rewritten to document the scoping; new contract tests on both languages (tests/test_model_config.py:411-445, tests/fast/test_schemas.py:151-162, go/internal/config/config_test.go:203-260) plus a drift guard TestDockerfileHarnessModelDefault (tests/test_model_config.py:603-629) that parses ENV HARNESS_MODEL= out of both Dockerfiles and pins the value to _OPENROUTER_AUTO_DEFAULT_MODEL, explicitly to prevent a repeat of the kimi drift. Trace: deployer env -> defaultModelFromEnv(runtime)/_default_model_from_env(runtime) -> resolve_runtime_models/fast_resolve_models -> per-role model fields -> CLI/model invocation. The scoping check sits at the narrowest point (the cascade), so both the main node, the fast node, and the planning default inherit it uniformly.
intent_gaps: Title promises 'Docker deploys run the promised OpenRouter default' but the HARNESS_MODEL scoping in _default_model_from_env/defaultModelFromEnv is unconditional - it changes env semantics for bare-metal, docker-compose, and Railway deployments too, not just Docker images. The PR description frames this as a Docker fix; it is a global config-semantics change.

Silent on the small_model switch: because HARNESS_MODEL also feeds opencode.json small_model interpolation (Dockerfile:57), baking deepseek-v4-flash-0731 instead of kimi-k2.6 changes what every OpenCode image consumer runs for small-model calls - including deployers who set HARNESS_MODEL specifically to pick their small model. No migration/acknowledgement in description or README.

Silent on breaking existing HARNESS_MODEL users: any deployment that set HARNESS_MODEL to steer claude_code or codex roles loses that behavior with no log, warning, or release-note migration step - roles silently fall back to runtime base defaults.

Go-side drift guard gap: the description claims 'a drift guard pinning the Dockerfiles' baked value', but TestDockerfileHarnessModelDefault lives only in the Python suite (tests/test_model_config.py:603-629). go/internal/config/config_test.go adds no Dockerfile guard, so the canonical Go check (cd go && make check) leaves go/Dockerfile unguarded if the suites are run in isolation.

README.md:406 deletes the prior explicit instruction that codex Docker deploys must set SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-5.3-codex, but does not tell previously-pinned deployers what they now get instead (codex auth-mode default) or that they may still want an explicit pin for non-default codex models; docs-following users change models without a stated upgrade path.

The diff also rewrites _default_planning_model's precedence docstring (swe_af/execution/schemas.py:780-813) to describe a runtime-aware planning default that is a PRIOR change, not this one - the description is silent about touching that function's documentation, which can mislead reviewers into thinking planning-default behavior changed here (it did not; it only inherits the new HARNESS_MODEL scoping via resolve_runtime_models at schemas.py:805-811).
unrelated_changes: No hard unrelated changes found; all 11 files serve the two stated fixes. Borderline items: (1) the docstring rewrite of _default_planning_model (swe_af/execution/schemas.py:780-813) documents the PREVIOUS commit's runtime-aware planning default and only needed a one-line cascade note - the larger reflow mixes prior-change documentation into this diff; (2) the .env.example AI_MODEL comment reflow (.env.example:82-88) is formatting-only beyond the scoping clarification; (3) README.md:406 also deletes the codex SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-5.3-codex deployment instruction, which is related but goes beyond what the title ('Docker deploys run the promised OpenRouter default') advertises.

For Codex with ChatGPT subscription auth, install the Codex CLI on the host, run `codex login`, leave `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset for this process, and set `SWE_CODEX_AUTH_MODE=chatgpt` or `auto`. For OpenAI API-platform billing, set `SWE_CODEX_AUTH_MODE=api_key` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
 
-> **Codex deployments using the Docker image must set `SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-5.3-codex` on the environment** (or pass `models: {"default": "gpt-5.3-codex"}` in every build's `config`). The image bakes `HARNESS_MODEL=openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6` as an OpenCode fallback, and SWE-AF's model-resolution env cascade reads `HARNESS_MODEL` — so without `SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL` set, the Codex CLI receives an OpenRouter model id it can't handle and the Product Manager reasoner fails in ~13s. Setting `SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL` makes the cascade pin every role to the Codex model.
+> The Docker image bakes `HARNESS_MODEL=openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` so OpenCode's `small_model` config interpolation always has a value. `HARNESS_MODEL` only affects the `open_code` runtime — `claude_code` and `codex` deployments resolve their own runtime defaults (codex picks its model by auth mode) and can override per role via `SWE_DEFAULT_MODEL` / `models` as usual.
 
 > Codex CLI's `workspace-write` sandbox uses bubblewrap (`bwrap`) and needs Linux user namespaces enabled on the host. Most production Linux hosts and managed container runtimes (Railway, etc.) allow this by default, but local Docker on WSL2 or hardened environments may refuse with `bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace`. If the verifier reports that error, the coder ran but couldn't write files — enable user namespaces on the host before relying on the codex runtime there.

+class TestDockerfileHarnessModelDefault(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Guard: the HARNESS_MODEL the images bake must be the OpenRouter auto
+    default the code and README promise. Docker layer caching plus the env
+    cascade means a drifted value silently becomes what every OpenRouter-only
+    deployment actually runs (that is exactly how kimi-k2.6 shipped)."""
+
+    def _dockerfile_value(self, relpath: str) -> str:
+        root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+        with open(os.path.join(root, relpath), encoding="utf-8") as fp:
+            for line in fp:
+                if line.startswith("ENV HARNESS_MODEL="):
+                    return line.strip().split("=", 1)[1]
+        raise AssertionError(f"no ENV HARNESS_MODEL line in {relpath}")
+
+    def test_python_image_matches_auto_default(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._dockerfile_value("Dockerfile"), _OPENROUTER_AUTO_DEFAULT_MODEL
+        )
+
+    def test_go_image_matches_auto_default(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._dockerfile_value(os.path.join("go", "Dockerfile")),
+            _OPENROUTER_AUTO_DEFAULT_MODEL,
+        )
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
